body.statement: Let all three budgets diverge and allow a sequence of compatible laws with \(w_{1,x}\to1\), \(w_{0,x}\to0\), \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)\to1\), and \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)\to0\).  Then \([L,R]\) converges to the binary-outcome Manski interval \(\left[\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x\},\;\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x\}\right]\).  No Manski-recovery claim is made at finite budgets or under latent positivity bounded away from zero.
body.justification: The all-budget limit locates the model between point identification and unrestricted treatment-response bounds without overstating finite-budget coverage.
body.gap: Imbens relates unrestricted sensitivity to worst-case bounds qualitatively; this proposition gives the exact common-binary-\(U\) endpoint limit and the required loss of latent positivity.
body.consumer: Users can interpret very large budgets against a familiar worst-case benchmark and detect implementations that converge to the wrong limit.
body.proof_tex:
First derive a budget-free outer bound from consistency alone.  In stratum \(x\), for some \(s_{1,x},s_{0,x}\in[0,1]\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde E\{Y(1)\mid X=x\}
&=p_xr_{1,x}+(1-p_x)s_{1,x},\\
\widetilde E\{Y(0)\mid X=x\}
&=(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+p_xs_{0,x}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore every compatible law, and in particular every law in every finite-budget common-(U) class, obeys
\[
p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x
\leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
\leq p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x.
\]
After weighting and summing, this gives a lower bound on \(L\) and an upper bound on \(R\) equal to the two claimed Manski endpoints.

It remains to show that both inequalities become attainable in the all-budget limit through the same binary confounder.  Along any sequence with \(\Gamma_{A,n},\Gamma_{0,n},\Gamma_{1,n}\to\infty\), choose in each stratum
\[
\varepsilon_n=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\Gamma_{A,n}}},
\qquad
w_{1,x}^{(n)}=1-\varepsilon_n,
\qquad
w_{0,x}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_n.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{OR}(w_{1,x}^{(n)},w_{0,x}^{(n)})
=\frac{(1-\varepsilon_n)^2}{\varepsilon_n^2}=\Gamma_{A,n},
\qquad
\pi_x^{(n)}\longrightarrow p_x.
\]
Bayes' rule consequently gives \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)\to1\) and \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)\to0\), so latent positivity vanishes along this sequence.

For the lower endpoint select \(\theta_{1,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{1,n}\) and \(\theta_{0,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{0,n}\).  In the treated mixture, \(w_{1,x}^{(n)}\to1\), so
\[
|\mu_{1,1,x}^{(n)}-r_{1,x}|
\leq1-w_{1,x}^{(n)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since \(\operatorname{odds}(\mu_{1,0,x}^{(n)})=operatorname{odds}(\mu_{1,1,x}^{(n)})/\Gamma_{1,n}\), interiority of \(r_{1,x}\) implies \(\mu_{1,0,x}^{(n)}\to0\).  In the control mixture, \(w_{0,x}^{(n)}\to0\), so \(\mu_{0,0,x}^{(n)}\to r_{0,x}\), while
\(\operatorname{odds}(\mu_{0,1,x}^{(n)})=Gamma_{0,n}\operatorname{odds}(\mu_{0,0,x}^{(n)})\) implies \(\mu_{0,1,x}^{(n)}\to1\).  Hence the common-pair lower contrast converges to
\[
p_xr_{1,x}-\{(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+p_x\}.
\]

For the upper endpoint select \(\theta_{1,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{1,n}^{-1}\) and \(\theta_{0,x}^{(n)}=\Gamma_{0,n}^{-1}\).  The same mixture argument gives
\[
\mu_{1,1,x}^{(n)}\to r_{1,x},\quad
\mu_{1,0,x}^{(n)}\to1,quad
\mu_{0,0,x}^{(n)}\to r_{0,x},\quad
\mu_{0,1,x}^{(n)}\to0,
\]
and therefore the common-pair upper contrast converges to
\[
p_xr_{1,x}+1-p_x-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}.
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) places \(L_n\) below the first feasible contrasts and \(R_n\) above the second, while the consistency bound places them on the opposite sides.  The squeeze theorem and the finite weighted sum over \(x\) prove convergence to the displayed interval.  The construction explicitly uses diverging budgets and propensities conditional on \(U\) tending to zero or one, so it yields no finite-budget or uniform-latent-positivity recovery claim.
